recipes.title: Pad Thai
recipes.description: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, bean sprouts, peanuts and a sweet-sour tamarind sauce.

ingredients.name: and 1 tablespoon (75 ml) palm sugar (or granulated sugar)
dried red chili pepper flakes (or to taste)
shrimp, tofu, chicken, squid, or beef

steps.instructionText: Soak the noodles in warm water for about 20 minutes and strain.
Alternatively, pour boiling water over the noodles and let them sit for 7 minutes.)
Mix the fish sauce with the vinegar, sugar and tamarind juice together in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok on high, and brown the chopped garlic and chili peppers for a minute.
Cook the meats/tofu in oil, until they are browned (6–8 minutes).
Add assorted veggies and cook until tender.
Add noodles. Crack the eggs over the noodles, allow them to cook, and then mix them up.
Add the fish sauce mix into the wok, mix it all up and turn the heat down to medium.
Add the chopped green onions and bean sprouts, then stir fry for 2 more minutes.
Serve on a large plate or bowl. Garnish with chopped peanuts and, optionally, chopped cilantro or coriander and a wedge of lime.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken simmered in coconut milk with green curry paste and lime leaves.

ingredients.name: Thai green curry paste (according to taste)
thick stalks lemongrass, fat ends bashed with a rolling pin
skinless, boneless chicken, cut into chunks
kaffir lime leaves, torn into pieces
good shake of Thai fish sauce or light soy sauce
small handful of coriander leaves, roughly chopped

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan.
Add the green curry paste and sugar and cook over a fairly high heat for about a minute, stirring with the lemongrass, if using.
Reduce the heat slightly and stir in the chicken pieces and lime leaves or zest until coated in the paste.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce or soy sauce and bring to a simmer, cooking for 25–30 minutes until thickened slightly.
Stir in the coriander and lime juice.
Check for seasoning, adding more fish sauce or soy sauce if needed.
Leave the curry to sit for a few minutes so the sauce becomes creamier. You will also taste the true flavours of the curry paste ingredients when it's slightly cooler.
Serve with lots of fragrant Thai jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Khao Pad Gai
recipes.description: Thai chicken fried rice with egg, tomato and fresh garnishes.

ingredients.name: large chicken breast, sliced in thin strips
cooked Thai jasmine rice, refrigerated overnight

steps.instructionText: Make sure that all of the ingredients are prepared and set aside in small bowls by the stove.
Add about 4 Tbsp peanut oil to the wok, and turn the flame to high heat.
When the oil is almost smoking, add the chicken strips and push around vigorously with a wok spoon or spatula.
When the chicken seems as if it is starting to brown, push it up the side of the wok and crack the eggs into the wok.
Stir the eggs around a bit. When almost fully scrambled, mix in the chicken and stir around for 30 seconds more.
Push the eggs/chicken to the side, add some more oil, and throw in the tomato and onion. Stir-fry for about 5 minutes. They will not look done, but in the end, they will be fine.
Add the cold cooked rice and mix it all in.
Turn the heat to low, then add a few splashes of fish sauce and soy sauce to taste.
Add sugar, salt, MSG, a splash of vinegar, and chili sauce if wanted. Lastly, add the fried garlic on top. Stir it all in and turn off the heat.
On a large platter, arrange the garnishes on a lettuce leaf, and plate the fried rice next to it.
Eat the garnishes with the fried rice.

recipes.title: Pattaya Fried Rice
recipes.description: Chicken and vegetable fried rice wrapped in a thin omelette.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. When the oil is hot, fry the garlic and shallots, stirring until brown and fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces, carrot, green peas, and red chilli. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, nam pla, tomato sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir until all mixed.
To make the omelette, heat the oil in a separate pan. Beat the eggs, and pour into the pan. Cook until the egg is browned on the bottom.
Flip the egg over to cook on the other side.
Place a ball of the fried rice mixture in the center of the omelette. Fold up the 4 edges of the omelette to enclose the rice. Flip it onto a serving plate.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)
recipes.description: Basic Thai egg fried rice with garlic, fish sauce and spring onion.

ingredients.name: cooked meat (e.g. shrimp, pork, chicken, etc.)

steps.instructionText: Heat up a frying pan or wok and add the oil, then the minced garlic. Stir fry until fragrant.
Add the eggs, and stir fry the eggs until cooked.
Add the rice and stir fry.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar, then continue frying until the rice is crumbly.
Add meat, pepper, and spring onions. Stir again until heated through, then transfer to a serving dish.

recipes.title: Pad Kra Pao Gai
recipes.description: Fiery minced chicken stir-fried with holy basil, chilli and green beans.

steps.instructionText: Add the oil to a pan over high heat. Wait until the oil has heated up.
One the oil is hot, add the chillis and garlic to the pan and stir fry for roughly 10 seconds.
Add the minced chicken, and stir fry with a spatula.
When the chicken is nearly done add the green beans.
Add the fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Stir fry for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat off, add basil, and stir for 5 seconds.
Serve with rice and a fried egg on top.

recipes.title: Pineapple Curry
recipes.description: Quick red curry with pineapple, coconut milk and shrimp.

steps.instructionText: Simmer the coconut milk in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes and add red curry paste.
Put the sliced pineapple in the curry and wait until it is soft.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then add the shrimp.
Flavor the curry by adding the palm sugar, fish sauce, and ripe tamarind. Add more palm sugar for a sweeter curry, add more fish sauce for a salty curry, and add more ripe tamarind for a sour flavor.

recipes.title: Tom Kha Kai
recipes.description: Thai coconut and galangal chicken soup with lemongrass and lime.

ingredients.name: stalks lemongrass, cut into 1-inch pieces or split
x 1-inch (5 x 2.5 cm) cube galangal, sliced thin
mini Thai bird chilies, finely chopped

steps.instructionText: Bring stock and coconut milk to a boil.
Add lemongrass, galangal, chilies, sugar, and pepper.
Add onion, tomato, chicken bits, and mushrooms.
Keep at a rolling boil for 4 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat.
Stir in lime juice and soy sauce.
Garnish with cilantro and chilies.

recipes.title: Tom Yum Gai
recipes.description: Hot and sour Thai chicken soup with lemongrass and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: fresh lemongrass stem, cut into short lengths
hot fresh Thai chilies, just broken with pestle

steps.instructionText: Place the stock in a pot, add the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, and bring to boil over medium heat.
Add the chicken meat, mushroom, fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar; cook slowly and uncovered for 10 minutes. Do not stir.
Add the tomatoes and chilies and cook for 5 more minutes. Remove from heat.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Thai Shrimp
recipes.description: Shrimp and peppers stir-fried in a sweet-spicy soy and chilli sauce.

steps.instructionText: Combine soy sauce, chili paste, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch, sesame oil and broth. Set aside.
Preheat a large sauté pan or wok over high heat. Add peanut oil and shrimp and stir-fry until shrimp is pink. Remove and keep warm.
Add bell pepper and garlic and stir-fry until bell pepper has taken on slight browning. Remove and keep warm.
Add liquid mixture to pan and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid has reduced to ¼ cup.
Add shrimp and vegetables back to pan and toss. Heat through.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately over rice or noodles.

recipes.title: Tod Mun (Thai Fish Cakes)
recipes.description: Fried Thai fish cakes with red curry paste and green beans.

ingredients.name: ground fish or fish paste (pla kuud)

steps.instructionText: Stack the lime leaves and roll them together into a tube shape. Slice them into thin strips.
Slice the green beans into small (½ inch) pieces.
Mince the fish.
Mix all the ingredients except the green beans and lime leaves in a bowl.
Stir until the mixture is smooth.
Add the green beans and lime leaves to the mixture and stir again.
Add the oil to a frying pan and heat to a medium temperature.
Drop a tablespoon of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly. When the bottom is cooked, turn over.
When cooked on both sides, place on a paper towel to drain any extra oil. Continue with the rest of the mixture.

recipes.title: Fuk-Thong Pad Khai
recipes.description: Pumpkin stir-fried with minced pork, egg and oyster sauce.

steps.instructionText: To prepare the pumpkin, remove seeds and cut off the outside skin of the pumpkin. Cut the pumpkin into 1-inch cubes and wash well with water.
Place pumpkin in a saucepan, and cover with water. Bring to the boil and cook until tender. When it is soft, drain the water.
Heat the oil in a pan, and fry the garlic until it becomes lightly browned and fragrant.
Add the minced pork to the pan, and let cook until the pork is nearly cooked through.
Add the cooked squash to the pork.
Crack the eggs into the pan.
Once the eggs are cooked, stir with pumpkin and minced pork.
Stir in the fish sauce, sugar, pepper, spring onion, and oyster sauce.
Serve with warm rice.

recipes.title: Thai Rice Balls in Coconut Milk
recipes.description: Chewy glutinous rice balls in sweet coconut cream.

steps.instructionText: Mix the rice flour with enough water to make a stiff paste, adding the pandan essence to the water before mixing with the rice flour. Knead well, then form the dough into pea-sized balls.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the rice balls, and remove them when they float to the surface. Drain.
Bring half the coconut cream to a boil, stirring constantly to prevent it from separating, then add the flour balls.
When the mixture returns to a boil, remove from heat and stir in the remaining coconut cream.
If serving this dish with eggs, in a separate saucepan bring water to a boil and reduce heat, then crack eggs one at a time into the water. When eggs are done, remove from water and set aside.
Serve as dessert in small bowls, adding one egg per bowl. Thais often add sweet corn kernels to the final product.

recipes.title: Coconut Pudding I
recipes.description: Chilled young-coconut pudding set with agar and milk.

steps.instructionText: Purée the young coconut flesh in a blender, and keep aside.
In a saucepan, combine the tender coconut water and china-grass strands. Heat gently until the china-grass strands melt completely.
In the meantime, heat milk and condensed milk in another saucepan over medium heat. Let it come to a boil.
To the boiled milk, add the melted china-grass mixture, and combine well.
Remove from the flame and let it cool down for at least 5 minutes.
Add the pureed tender coconut to the cooled milk mixture, and mix everything well.
Pour the mixture into a cake pan or stainless steel pan.
Place the pudding in the freezer for about 15 minutes or until it begins to set.
Remove the pudding from the freezer and place it in the refrigerator until fully set.
Using a knife, gently cut the pudding and serve it in dessert bowls.

recipes.title: Tub Tim Krob
recipes.description: Water chestnut jewels in a tapioca coat, served in coconut milk.

steps.instructionText: Peel and cut the water chestnuts into small cubes.
Soak the water chestnut cubes in red food coloring until their color changes to red.
Mix the colored water chestnut cubes with tapioca flour until the skin of the cubes is covered with the flour.
Boil them in hot water for several minutes or until the water chestnut cubes float to the top of the water.
Mix the water chestnut cubes with coconut milk and serve with ice cubes in a bowl.

recipes.title: Thai Lemonade
recipes.description: Lemongrass and ginger syrup topped with sparkling water.

ingredients.name: cm piece of ginger, peeled and cut into pieces

steps.instructionText: Bring the water to a boil with the sugar, lemon grass, and ginger. Boil for 20 minutes.
Allow the syrup to cool, then remove lemongrass and ginger.
Pour the syrup in 4 large glasses, and add the carbonated water.
Garnish glasses with lime discs.

recipes.title: Chuu Chee Fish
recipes.description: Whole fried fish under a thick chu chee curry and coconut sauce.

steps.instructionText: In a wok or large frypan, over high heat, fry fish using most of the vegetable oil, until golden on one side. It will take about 5 minutes.
Lower heat and, using tongs, gently turn fish over.
Turn up heat again and cook until golden. Using tongs again, lift fish gently onto a serving plate.
In the wok, gently stir-fry the curry-paste and lime leaves in remaining tablespoon of oil.
Add coconut milk and fish sauce. Simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add sugar and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Taste to see if extra coconut milk, fish sauce, or sugar is required.
Pour sauce over fish and garnish with cilantro and chopped chili peppers.

recipes.title: Khanom Mo Keang (Thai Custard)
recipes.description: Baked Thai custard of mung beans, egg and coconut with crispy shallots.

ingredients.name: large shallot, peeled and thinly sliced
large whole chicken eggs plus 3 yolks (or 5 duck eggs)

steps.instructionText: Put the shallot slices and oil into a small frying pan over medium-low heat. Stir the shallot slices, until they are golden brown and crispy.
Grease the bottom and sides of a 9×13-inch baking pan. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Soften the palm or coconut sugar in a pan over medium heat.
Blend the mung beans, eggs, both sugars, coconut cream, salt, and any leftover oil from the shallots together until smooth.
Let the custard mixture sit for 5 minutes until it becomes less frothy.

Pour the custard mixture into the pan. Place the pan on a rack positioned in the upper third of the oven. Bake at 180°C for 35–45 minutes or until the center is slightly firm and the top is golden brown.
Put some of the fried shallots over the top of the custard.

recipes.title: Kanom Piak Poon
recipes.description: Steamed-style pandan and coconut pudding, cut into squares.

steps.instructionText: Combine the rice flour, arrowroot, and lime water. Stir in the sugar, water, pandan juice, coconut milk, and salt until the sugar dissolves. Strain this mixture into a brass pan or pot to remove any solids.
Heat the pan over low heat. Stir the mixture continuously over low heat to keep it from sticking to the bottom of the pan.
Cook until the mixture is glossy and thickened. This will take about 30–40 minutes.
Pour the mixture into an oiled mold. Smooth the top, then let rest until cool.
When the pudding is cooled, use a knife to cut into the desired shape. Serve with grated coconut.
